prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1372; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact collision at an intersection. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the driver's policy declarations. The claimant is named as a driver on the policy, and the coverage period was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver. All three describe the collision the same way as the claimant did, and the photos taken at the scene are consistent with that account.

Entry 4: Police and witnesses both confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. No record shows any prior damage to the vehicle, and the repair estimate was requested.

Entry 5: Received the medical records describing a shoulder injury. The nature of the injury and the force of the impact appear to fit well together. Our file shows no earlier injury to the same area.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits gradually decreasing as the claimant's condition improved. The provider's notes reflect steady progress.

Entry 7: Claimant contacted our office to add a few minor details about the sequence of events. The core account did not change from the original statement, and the additions were consistent with the physical evidence.

Entry 8: Reviewed the damage report with the repair appraiser. It is not yet clear whether every area of damage resulted from this impact, so the appraiser will inspect the vehicle further before finalizing the estimate.

Entry 9: Reviewed the medical treatment timeline against the records on file. Nothing in the file suggests the damage or injury occurred before the coverage period started.

Entry 10: Referred the file for final evaluation of the bodily injury and property damage components. Further correspondence will be directed to the claimant's attorney.
